A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same bandit reduction and core regret guarantees. All 19 pages of each version, including their appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports algorithms, theoretical guarantees and proofs, including Appendices A–E. It contains no original experimental, simulation, user-study or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v3 likewise reports theoretical algorithms and proofs, including Appendices A–D, without original empirical results. Table 1 compares theoretical guarantees.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1's exact vertex decomposition and normal-cone policy selection are replaced by Frank–Wolfe PolicyDecomposition and uniform sampling of the resulting policies. This changes action execution to an approximate construction requiring linear optimization oracles. The robust continuous-exponential-weights algorithm itself is retained, renumbered from Algorithm 2 to Algorithm 3.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirically evaluates tasks. The broader action-set applicability in v3 is a theoretical generalization, not added evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version experimentally evaluates comparison methods. Table 1 retains the same theoretical comparators, including Neu and Valko (2014), Dai et al. (2023), and both Liu et al. (2023) entries.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental protocols. The revised oracle requirements and decomposition iteration budget specify the proposed algorithm, not evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity studies, robustness tests or case studies. Misspecification robustness is established through theoretical analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty intervals or significance tests. The retained concentration bounds are theoretical guarantees.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. Table 1 retains the regret rates; revised computational guarantees and appendix proof constants are theoretical changes addressed under T1 and R1.

T1.justification: v3 formalizes oracle access and normalization, adds proofs of the Minkowski-sum identity and the 2/sqrt(M) policy-approximation bound, and removes v2's vertex/normal-cone and linear-programming lemmas. Appendix C.4 incorporates approximation error, increasing epsilon's coefficient from 4 to 6 while preserving final regret rates. Appendix A also corrects 'is the boundary' to 'lies on the boundary'.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction broaden the computational contribution from poly(d,C,T) time using explicit constraint descriptions to poly(d,T) overhead plus polynomially many oracle calls. The polynomial-constraint restriction on the combinatorial-bandit claim is removed. The headline regret and simulator small-loss bounds remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 identifies efficient-oracle action sets with exponentially many constraints, such as spanning trees, as a computational limitation and leaves oracle-only efficiency open. v3 removes this limitation and open question while retaining the two regret/small-loss questions. The adaptive-adversary extension discussed in v2's Section 2.1 footnote is also removed.

D1.justification: v3 specifies fixed oracle tie-breaking, PolicyDecomposition initialization, 1/j averaging and the M=N iteration choice. These replace the constraint-specific implementation instructions in v2 Section 4. The continuous-exponential-weights parameters are retained, and neither version provides code or experimental resource information.

R1.justification: The comparison with Neu and Valko (2014) shifts from acknowledging a constraint-dependent computational disadvantage to claiming oracle efficiency while retaining the regret and feedback advantages. Table 1 changes their stated oracle count from T to poly(d,T). Appendix A updates the computational comparison with Hanna et al.; Schneider (2014) and Wei et al. (2021) replace the Schrijver (1986) and Weibel (2007) references.

P1.justification: Section 3.2 is rewritten around approximate policy mixtures. The standalone Computational Complexity section and linear-programming appendix are removed, with oracle implementation integrated into Section 3 and new proof subsections. The remaining sections and appendices are reorganized, although much of the retained proof prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 uses a wider text block and different title/abstract styling throughout. v2's normal-cone Figure 1 is removed, a PolicyDecomposition algorithm box is added, and Table 1 receives a shortened caption and merged computation cells. These constitute substantial layout and display revisions.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses v2's explicit computational restriction and corresponding open question by providing an oracle-based policy construction with a proved approximation bound (Algorithms 1–2 and Appendices C.2/C.4). This substantially broadens applicability while retaining the regret guarantees. The tradeoff from exact to approximate execution is explicitly controlled in the revised proof, substantiating the stronger computational contribution.
